considered_rates.assessment: US 10Y 4.94 is 5y percentile 99.40 / 1y z 2.48 and AU 10Y 5.202 is 5y percentile 99.88 — real statistical stretch. AU housing is a genuine duration-normalization catalyst, but AU observations are 2026-09-09 (age_days 8), so post-FOMC AU yields are unknown and cannot be traded from this packet. US duration is current (2026-09-17) but the inflation mechanism has not broken: US inflation gauge 72, August CPI kept a tightening bias, PPI accelerated, import prices added nonfuel pressure, Michigan inflation expectations rose. Research method: stretch without a weakening inflation mechanism is a yardstick, not a long-bond signal. Post-hike US 10Y/2Y already -7bp on 2026-09-17; some of the obvious mean-reversion print has started.

US 2s10s 27bp is 1y percentile 1.39 / 1y z -2.30 after a -25bp 1m flatten, but 5y percentile is 56.1 — a one-year extreme, not a five-year dislocation. CA 2s10s 57bp is 1y percentile 0.79 with the same 5y-mid problem (5y percentile 65.7). A post-hike steepener is a plausible tactical, not the cleaner 5y mean-reversion in this packet.

CA-US 5Y -122bp is 1y percentile 0.20 / 1y z -1.91 (10Y 1y percentile 1.79). That is a stretched spread, but CA labor 38 vs US 75 and CA inflation 55 vs US 72 justify Canada yielding less; 5y percentiles (CA-US 5Y 7.35, 10Y 11.4) are cheap, not 99.96-style extremes. BoC energy pass-through is a reason the gap may have gone too far, yet Canada August CPI at 3% with core near 2% does not force CA yields up. AU-US 2Y +40.5bp is 1y percentile 47 — not stretched on the live 1y window. AU-NZ RV is explicitly unavailable (RBNZ 403). Do not force a rates RV when the 5y mispricing lives in spot AUDNZD.

NZDNOK 5y z -2.26 is a cheap-NZD extreme with an oil-tail-fade catalyst, but Norway has no gauges or rates in the packet. AUDUSD is not extreme enough to fade on this remit.

trade.structure: outright spot short (sell AUD / buy NZD)
trade.thesis: AUDNZD is the packet’s most stretched G10 cross (5y percentile 99.96, 5y z 2.96, 1y percentile 99.80) after a +2.94% one-month run. The move is not a verified AU-NZ rate-gap trade: NZ official yields are unavailable, AUDUSD is only 1y 75th / 5y 84th, and NZDUSD is already cheap (1y 21st / 5y 11th). The dislocation is relative AUD richness versus NZD. The reversal condition is a local Australian housing break (NSW stamp duty -24% YoY, transactions -18%, Sydney/Melbourne values >7% off peak) against still-hot AU inflation pricing, plus New Zealand’s India FTA covering ~95% of NZ exports as new NZD-supportive information. Mean reversion here is not ‘price went up’; it is a 5y extreme whose AU high-yield/NZ-weakness narrative is now colliding with a transmission-channel break on the AUD leg and a positive trade shock on the NZD leg.
why_now: AUDNZD printed a fresh 5y extreme on 2026-09-17, one day after the housing and NZ-India news dated 2026-09-16, with 1d still +0.09% — stretch intact, catalysts live.
The Sep 16 Fed 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% was >90% priced into the decision; the global rates impulse is known information, not a new reason to extend AUD versus NZD.
AU housing evidence is the missing local falsifier of the ‘AU can keep 99th-percentile yields and a 5y-rich cross’ narrative.
NZ-India FTA is independent, same-week NZD-positive news that the 1m AUDNZD squeeze has not yet mean-reverted.
AUDCAD is a worse fade: CA-AU 2Y -167.5bp (5y z -1.68) still points the same way as spot. AUDNZD does not have that confirmed rate support.

what_changes_my_mind: An official AU-NZ 2Y/10Y gap that is itself at a comparable 5y extreme would convert this from spot fade to ‘rates already own it’ and I would stand down.
AU housing volumes/prices reversing higher while NZ activity/labor keep sliding would mean the AUD transmission channel is not breaking.
A live executable AUDNZD print well off the 5y extreme before entry would remove the stretch that this seat is paid to fade.
why_now: The 5y stretch is live on 2026-09-17 while the housing and FTA items printed 2026-09-16 and have not yet pulled the cross off the extreme.
The Fed hike was pre-priced (>90% for 25bp); it is not new information that should extend a 5y AUDNZD outlier.
Fading AUDCAD instead would fight a still-supportive CA-AU yield gap; AUDNZD does not have that problem in the packet.
